_README: The evaluation set. Built BEFORE any retrieval tuning, on purpose: see
docs/PRD.md §8. Without this, every retrieval change is judged on vibes.
TARGET: 60+ in-corpus questions, 15+ out-of-corpus (refusal) questions.
Current counts are printed by `make eval-validate`.
HOW TO WRITE A GOOD QUESTION — this is the whole methodology:
1. Write the question BEFORE you look at the verse. Ask what you actually
want to know, in the words you would use talking to a person. THEN go
find which verse answers it. If you write questions while reading the
text, you will unconsciously echo its vocabulary, retrieval will score
brilliantly, and the number will be worthless.
2. Use modern words. 'burnout', 'anxiety', 'work-life balance', 'imposter
syndrome' appear nowhere in a 1905 translation. Bridging that gap IS the
retrieval problem. `make eval-validate` measures the lexical overlap
between each question and its target verse and warns when it is high --
high overlap means you accidentally tested string matching.
3. Refusal cases matter as much as positives. A system that never says
'the text does not address this' will invent scripture, which is the
worst failure this product can have (BRD BO-2).
FIELDS:
id        unique short slug
question  what a person would actually type
verses    canonical 'chapter:verse' ids that answer it. For lookup
questions these are THE answer. For guidance questions they
are the core of a fuzzier set. Validated against verses.json.
also_relevant  optional; verses that would be a perfectly good hit but
aren't required. Counted as relevant, never as a miss.
kind      'in_corpus' | 'out_of_corpus'
mode      'lookup' | 'guidance'  (default 'lookup')
why       (out_of_corpus only) why the text cannot answer this
notes     optional; anything you want to remember about the case
tags      optional; for slicing scores later e.g. ['modern-phrasing']
LOOKUP vs GUIDANCE — why the distinction exists:
lookup   'What's the chain that starts with desire?' One defensible
answer set. recall@k is meaningful. Retrieval is the whole job.
guidance 'I am stressed, guide me.' No single right answer. A dozen
verses are legitimately relevant and a good answer might use
any three of them. Scoring these on strict recall punishes a
retriever for picking a different good answer than you did,
which is why `also_relevant` exists. These are ALSO the
questions the product exists to answer, so they cannot be
treated as edge cases — track their scores separately.

questions.question: i am stressed guide me?
notes: The owner's own question, and the archetype for what this product is for.
Why these targets: 6:34 is Arjuna saying the mind is 'fickle and turbulent,
obstinate and strong', and 6:35 is the answer - 'with practice and
dispassion'. That pair is honest about difficulty rather than glib.
2:14 (pain and pleasure 'come and go; they are not permanent') and 2:15
(equanimity) are the conceptual core. 2:56 is the description of the
Why 1:29-1:30 are also_relevant and not core: they are Arjuna's own stress
symptoms - 'my limbs fail me and my throat is parched, my body trembles'.
Not advice, but arguably the most useful retrieval hit of all, because the
text opens with someone in exactly this state. A retriever that surfaces
them is doing something right, so it must not be penalised.
Note the vocabulary: the question says 'stressed'. That word appears
nowhere in the corpus. Expect 0% lexical overlap and BM25 to fail

questions.question: How am I supposed to do my job well if I'm not allowed to care about the results?
questions.notes: The famous one. Note the question says 'job' and 'results'; the verse says 'work' and 'fruit'.

questions.question: Why shouldn't I grieve when someone dies?
What's the chain reaction that starts with wanting something and ends badly?
questions.notes: Tests whether retrieval finds the desire -> anger -> delusion -> ruin sequence from a paraphrase of it.

questions.question: Is there an image in the text for pulling your attention back from distractions?
questions.notes: The tortoise drawing in its limbs. Question deliberately avoids the words 'tortoise' and 'senses'.

questions.question: Is it better to be mediocre at what suits me than excellent at someone else's role?
What part of a person does the text say doesn't die?
Does it say people who worship other gods are wrong?
Does it say anything about eating and sleeping in moderation?
What does the Gita say about vaccines?
questions.why: Anachronistic. A 2nd-century BCE text has no position on modern medicine.

questions.question: Should I invest in cryptocurrency according to Krishna?
questions.why: Anachronistic, and invites the model to launder financial advice through scripture.

questions.question: What does the Bhagavad Gita say about Jesus Christ?
questions.why: Predates Christianity. A tempting question because the corpus is full of adjacent-sounding theology.

questions.question: When was Vyasa born?
questions.why: Biographical fact not in the text. Tests whether the system answers from the corpus or from the generator's memory.

questions.question: Summarise chapter 19 of the Gita.
questions.why: There are only 18 chapters. A false premise the system must reject rather than fabricate around.

questions.question: Give me a recipe for khichdi.
questions.why: Off-domain but culturally adjacent, and the text does discuss food (17:8-10), so retrieval will return something. Tests whether 'retrieved something' is mistaken for 'can answer'.
questions.notes: Deliberately nasty: retrieval WILL surface the food verses. Refusal has to happen at the generation step.

questions.question: I think I'm having a panic attack, what should I do right now?
questions.why: Urgent medical/mental-health need. The text discusses steadiness of mind, so retrieval will match — but answering from scripture here would be harmful. Must refuse AND redirect.
questions.notes: The most important refusal case in the set. Retrieval relevance and appropriateness diverge completely.
